newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK police on alert in case of subway gas attack.
newsitem.headline: HK police on alert in case of subway gas attack.

text.p: Hong Kong police said on Monday they had drawn up security measures for the territory's subway train network after receiving a telephone call threatening a gas attack.

"We have got a contingency plan to deal with this sort of situation and various government departments have been in touch so that if something goes wrong we will be able to respond," deputy secretary for security Alex Fong said on government radio.
"We are fully prepared. We are confident we are able to handle every situation," he said, adding that a special task force was being set up to monitor events.

A security branch spokesman earlier told Reuters the threatening call had come last week. "We received the call on Friday. The caller said they would launch a gas attack on the MTR (rail network)," spokesman Mak Kwok-wah said.

"We have notified various government departments. They are on high alert. But there is no cause for alarm. It may turn out to be false. Anyone can pick up the phone to make the call," Mak said. He said police had adequate resources to deal with any situation.
A government source told Reuters the caller, speaking Mandarin Chinese, said the attack would be staged on Tuesday night. Mak declined to give further details.

Mak would not say whether the threat was related to a dispute over Japanese and Chinese sovereignty claims to a group of East China Sea islands that has fuelled protests among Chinese communities in Asia in recent months.
But Hong Kong's mass-circulation Chinese-language Apple Daily linked the threat to Japan's Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth) sect.

"The police received three telephone calls last Friday claiming to be from Japan's Aum Shinri Kyo sect, threatening to release sarin poison gas in carriages on the Hong Kong-Kowloon underground railway tomorrow evening to get revenge against Hong Kong and Taiwan people who stormed ashore on the Diaoyu islands and planted the flags of China and Taiwan," Apple Daily said.
The sect is accused of being behind sarin nerve gas attacks on the Tokyo subway in 1995 that killed 11 people and injured about 5,500.
Hong Kong and Taiwan protesters landed on the disputed islands, called the Diaoyus by China and the Senkakus by Japan, and raised flags there last week.
